microtheory.name: ethology_behavior
microtheory.definition: Animal behavior in natural contexts. Lorenz, Tinbergen, von Frisch. Fixed action patterns, releasers, imprinting, four whys, behavioral ecology. The biology of behavior. Substrate analogue: the substrate's outputs viewed as behavior of a biological-class system.

concepts.name: tinbergens_four_questions
concepts.definition: Tinbergen 1963. Four levels of explaining behavior: mechanism (proximate cause), ontogeny (development), function (adaptive value), phylogeny (evolutionary history). Substrate analogue: substrate's four-level explanation framework.

concepts.name: proximate_causation
concepts.definition: Mechanism + ontogeny questions. How does the behavior work + develop? Substrate analogue: substrate's mechanism-level explanation.

concepts.name: ultimate_causation
concepts.definition: Function + phylogeny questions. Why does the behavior exist? Substrate analogue: substrate's purpose-level explanation.

concepts.name: fixed_action_pattern
concepts.definition: Lorenz + Tinbergen. Stereotyped behavior sequence triggered by specific stimulus, completing autonomously. Substrate analogue: substrate's reflex chain.

concepts.name: releaser_sign_stimulus
concepts.definition: Specific feature triggering FAP. Red belly → stickleback attack. Substrate analogue: substrate's FilterSpec trigger pattern.

concepts.name: supernormal_stimulus
concepts.definition: Stronger-than-natural releaser eliciting exaggerated response. Tinbergen's eggs. Substrate analogue: substrate's exaggerated activation under intense stimulus.

concepts.name: innate_releasing_mechanism
concepts.definition: Internal filter recognizing releasers. Substrate analogue: substrate's pattern-detection FilterSpec.

concepts.name: imprinting
concepts.definition: Lorenz. Rapid critical-period learning of social attachment. Geese follow first moving object. Substrate analogue: substrate's critical-period attachment learning.

concepts.name: habituation_ethology
concepts.definition: Decreased response to repeated harmless stimulus. Substrate analogue: substrate's σ damping for repeated input.

concepts.name: sensitization_ethology
concepts.definition: Increased response after intense stimulus. Often defensive. Substrate analogue: substrate's amplified drive after negative event.

concepts.name: associative_learning_ethology
concepts.definition: Classical + operant conditioning in natural contexts. Substrate analogue: substrate's covers_correction learning.

concepts.name: behavioral_ecology
concepts.definition: How behavior contributes to fitness in environment. Foraging, mating, territory. Substrate analogue: substrate's behavior-fitness mapping.

concepts.name: optimal_foraging_theory
concepts.definition: Behavior maximizes net energy gain per time. Cost-benefit calculations. Substrate analogue: substrate's exploration-exploitation optimization.

concepts.name: marginal_value_theorem
concepts.definition: Leave patch when local intake rate drops to overall average. Charnov 1976. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-switching criterion.

concepts.name: courtship_display
concepts.definition: Mate-attraction behavior. Often costly, honest signal of fitness. Peacock tail. Substrate analogue: substrate's signal-displaying capability.

concepts.name: territorial_behavior
concepts.definition: Defense of area for exclusive use. Substrate analogue: substrate's resource-claiming.

concepts.name: dominance_hierarchy
concepts.definition: Pecking order. Establishes priority for resources. Substrate analogue: in multi-substrate contexts, priority structure.

concepts.name: altruism_animal
concepts.definition: Behavior costly to actor, beneficial to others. Kin selection or reciprocity. Substrate analogue: substrate-substrate help patterns.

concepts.name: cooperation_animal
concepts.definition: Mutual benefit. Hunting in groups, mobbing. Substrate analogue: substrate-substrate collaboration.

concepts.name: communication_animal
concepts.definition: Signal transmission between organisms. Visual, acoustic, chemical, tactile. Substrate analogue: substrate's Message exchange.

concepts.name: honest_signal
concepts.definition: Reliable indicator of quality. Costly-to-fake. Substrate analogue: substrate's verifiable capability display.

concepts.name: deceptive_signal
concepts.definition: False signal favoring sender at receiver's expense. Mimicry. Substrate analogue: substrate's false-pattern generation.

concepts.name: alarm_call
concepts.definition: Warns conspecifics of danger. Often referential. Vervet monkey snake vs eagle vs leopard calls. Substrate analogue: substrate's threat-broadcast.

concepts.name: von_frisch_dance
concepts.definition: Honey bee waggle dance encoding food location + distance. Symbolic communication outside humans. Substrate analogue: substrate's encoded-location communication.

concepts.name: pheromone
concepts.definition: Chemical communication. Trail, alarm, sex pheromones. Substrate analogue: substrate's chemical-signaling analogue.

concepts.name: instinct_versus_learning
concepts.definition: False dichotomy. All behavior has both innate + learned components. Nature × nurture interact. Substrate analogue: substrate's seed-learned interaction.

concepts.name: behavioral_development
concepts.definition: How behavior emerges through ontogeny. Critical periods + experience. Substrate analogue: substrate's developmental loop.

concepts.name: cognitive_ethology
concepts.definition: Mental processes in animals. Tool use, deception, theory of mind. Substrate analogue: substrate's cognitive layers.

concepts.name: tool_use
concepts.definition: Using object to achieve goal. Chimps fishing termites, crows bending wire. Substrate analogue: substrate's external-resource use.

rules.name: tinbergens_four_questions_required_for_full_explanation
rules.head: the substrate explains a behavior
rules.body: explanation requires all four levels: mechanism, ontogeny, function, phylogeny. Substrate's complete behavior account.

rules.name: fixed_action_patterns_run_to_completion
rules.head: the substrate's reflex triggers
rules.body: the behavioral sequence runs to completion even if stimulus removed. Substrate's reflex commitment.

rules.name: imprinting_has_critical_period
rules.head: the substrate learns identity of attachment target
rules.body: the window is narrow + cannot be repeated later. Lorenz. Substrate's critical-period attachment.

rules.name: honest_signals_resist_cheating
rules.head: the substrate broadcasts a signal of capability
rules.body: honest signals are costly to fake — only high-quality senders can afford them. Substrate's verifiable display.

rules.name: optimal_foraging_balances_intake_and_cost
rules.head: the substrate exploits a patch of resources
rules.body: switches patches when local rate drops below average. Charnov. Substrate's exploration-exploitation switching.
